about: Noise: how AI turns static into pictures (diffusion). A puzzle film: find the cat in this static. Training adds noise to real pictures and teaches the model to guess it; generation runs that backwards about 50 times while the prompt steers each step. Factory #5. Narration-led: the voice is recorded first and every visual beat is keyed to its word times.

lines.text: Find the cat in this static.
lines.say: Find the cat, in this static.

lines.text: You can't. But AI image generators can. How?
Here's the trick: they learned it backwards.
Take a real photo. Sprinkle in a little static.
Then more, and more, until it's pure noise.
One job: guess which static you added.
After hundreds of millions of pictures, it gets really good.
Now flip it. Start from pure static.
Wipe away a little noise. Then again. Often about 50 times.
lines.say: Wipe away a little noise. Then again. Often about fifty times.

lines.text: Your prompt steers every step toward a cat.
Now type 'dog' instead? You get a dog.
lines.say: Now type dog, instead? You get a dog.

lines.text: The cat was never hiding. It was painted in.
So what's hiding in this static? One word. Go.
